stories.title: JEE Main 2027 registration numbers climb
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency reports over 5.72 lakh registrations for JEE Main 2027 Session 1, with 4.07 lakh candidates having completed fee payments. The application window remains open until November 22. The agency continues to track the figures as the January exam dates approach.

stories.title: NTA sets November 22 deadline for JEE Main
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency has reminded candidates to complete their JEE Main 2027 Session 1 applications by November 22. The agency advises using DigiLocker or JanParichay credentials to avoid biometric discrepancies. Over 5.72 lakh students have registered so far, with 4.07 lakh having paid their fees.

stories.title: NTA urges JEE Main applicants to finish forms
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency has advised JEE Main 2027 Session 1 applicants to complete their online formalities before the November 22 deadline. With 5.72 lakh registrations and 4.07 lakh fee payments recorded, the agency is encouraging students to download their confirmation pages to avoid incomplete applications.

stories.title: NTA clarifies NRI registration for JEE Main
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency has introduced a specific registration option for Non-Resident Indian candidates who do not possess an Aadhaar card. These applicants may now register using a valid Indian passport. The deadline for all Session 1 applications remains November 22, 2026.

stories.title: Bihar Board opens free coaching registration
stories.summary: The Bihar School Examination Board has opened registration for its free JEE and NEET coaching programme for the 2027-29 session. Eligible Class 10 students may apply online until November 19, 2026. The programme includes residential and non-residential options, with a selection test scheduled for December 6.

stories.title: Germany and Ireland gain popularity for students
stories.summary: Data from the Deutscher Akademischer Austauschdienst suggests that Indian students are increasingly choosing Germany and Ireland for higher education. Karan Lalit of TOEFL and GRE noted that these destinations have gained prominence over the USA, UK, Canada, and Australia during the past two years.

stories.title: Canada to make rural immigration pilot permanent
stories.summary: Canada will transition its Rural Community Immigration Pilot into a permanent residency programme starting January 1, 2027. The initiative aims to address labour shortages across 14 participating communities. Applicants must secure a job offer and a community recommendation to qualify for the new pathway.

stories.title: Illinois faces economic impact from visa shifts
stories.summary: Illinois could lose over 190 million dollars in economic activity this school year as visa rules for international students tighten. The report highlights concerns regarding the future of F-1 and H-1B visa holders. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: US State Department targets visa fraud
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department has identified multiple fraud operations involving fake staffing firms and forged academic records. The agency is intensifying scrutiny of employment and student visa programmes, citing cases where fraudsters used sham companies to cheat the system. Enforcement actions are currently underway.

stories.title: UK to adjust immigration rules in 2027
stories.summary: The UK government plans to update immigration policies in 2027, including potential changes to Skilled Worker salary thresholds and Graduate visa durations. The measures aim to attract highly skilled international talent while adjusting the national framework. The full details of the proposed changes remain forthcoming.

stories.title: Visa rule change leaves traveller out of pocket
stories.summary: Meg Green, a British national, says a change in Australian visa rules forced her to leave the country and reapply from overseas. The process left her $6,500 out of pocket. She had arrived on a working holiday visa in 2023 before planning to transition to student status.

stories.title: Visa policy shifts strand British expats in Bali
stories.summary: Meg Green, 28, is currently in Bali after new Australian visa regulations prevented her from remaining in the country. Green had spent three years in Australia and was enrolled in an IT diploma program. The policy shift has interrupted her plans to pursue a career in cybersecurity.

stories.title: University paperwork error affects students
stories.summary: International students at a Kansas university are facing delays due to a reported paperwork error. The institution has not provided further details regarding the administrative issue. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: NRI candidates can apply for JEE Main 2027 without Aadhaar
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency has updated registration for JEE Main 2027. Non-Resident Indian candidates who do not possess an Aadhaar card may now use a valid Indian passport to complete their application through a designated registration option. The agency is now accepting these alternative credentials.

stories.title: Boston University leaders oppose proposed OPT fee
stories.summary: Boston University President Melissa Gilliam and Provost Colin Duckett have objected to a proposed $70,000 fee for international students using the federal Optional Practical Training program. The leaders argue the cost would shrink student numbers, harming the university and local employers. The proposal is currently under review.

stories.title: Storage company offers student scholarships
stories.summary: The Storage Center is accepting applications for its Space to Succeed Scholarship until November 30. The program will award $5,000 to three students nationwide for community leadership. The company has granted $45,000 to nine students since the scholarship launched in early 2025.

stories.title: Commonwealth Shared Scholarships open for 2026
stories.summary: The Commonwealth Shared Scholarships programme is accepting applications for its 2026 intake until December 8. The fully funded awards support students from least developed and middle-income countries pursuing 12-month Master's degrees at participating UK universities. Applicants must apply directly through the institutions for initial selection.

stories.title: UK opens Commonwealth scholarships for international students
stories.summary: The British High Commission in Nigeria has announced that the Commonwealth Shared Scholarships programme is open for international postgraduate students. The fully funded initiative covers 12-month Master's degrees at UK universities. Interested applicants must apply through participating institutions before the December 8, 2026 deadline.

stories.title: Bet9ja Foundation announces 2027 undergraduate scholarships
stories.summary: The Bet9ja Foundation has opened applications for its 2027 undergraduate scholarship for students at Nigerian public universities. The program offers full tuition support for fields including law, medicine, and STEM. Applicants must meet specific academic and study-level requirements to qualify for the funding.

stories.title: Applications open for Vylor Agritech scholarship
stories.summary: The Vylor Agritech Scholarship Programme is accepting applications until November 30. The initiative provides up to Rs 35,000 per year to students pursuing agriculture-related degrees at government institutions. Applicants must have a family income not exceeding Rs 6,00,000 to be eligible for the financial support.

stories.title: Rolls-Royce opens engineering scholarship for women
stories.summary: Rolls-Royce India is accepting applications for the Wings4Her scholarship for female engineering students. The program supports those in their first or second year at AICTE-recognised institutions with family incomes under Rs 4 lakhs. The company aims to assist students demonstrating academic merit and financial need.

stories.title: Japan opens GRIPS 2027-28 scholarship applications
stories.summary: The National Graduate Institute for Policy Studies in Tokyo has opened applications for its 2027-28 academic programmes. Indian students can apply for master's and doctoral pathways in fields such as public policy and economics. The institute also lists external scholarship schemes for international applicants.

stories.title: GCWUS urges students to apply for provincial scholarship
stories.summary: Government College Women University Sialkot has directed eligible students to apply for the Chief Minister Punjab Honhaar Undergraduate Scholarship Program 2026. The university is urging students to review the criteria and submit their online applications promptly to secure financial support for their higher education.

stories.title: University of Macerata to offer international scholarships
stories.summary: The University of Macerata in Italy plans to open international admissions for the 2027-2028 academic year in November 2026. While the university has mentioned potential scholarship opportunities, it has not yet confirmed the details of its new competition. Admissions cover bachelor's and master's programmes.

stories.title: Parkes Shire Council opens scholarship applications
stories.summary: The Parkes Shire Council will open applications for the 2027 Jack Scoble Scholarships on November 16. The annual fund supports local students pursuing further education and training. The scholarships are intended to assist with costs for residents who demonstrate a commitment to their studies and community.

stories.title: UTEP announces full-ride engineering scholarship
stories.summary: The University of Texas at El Paso has opened applications for the Loya Scholarship, which covers full tuition, housing, food, and transportation. Recipients also receive a $1,000 monthly stipend and a $30,000 bonus upon graduation. The deadline for high school seniors to apply is January 31, 2027.

stories.title: UIS students eligible for French engineering scholarship
stories.summary: Industrial and mechanical engineering students at the Industrial University of Santander can apply for the 2027-2028 France Excellence Eiffel Scholarship. The program facilitates academic exchanges and dual-degree opportunities at the École Nationale d’Ingénieurs de Metz. Applications are managed through the university's international relations office.

stories.title: Indian universities climb global rankings
stories.summary: Indian institutions are rising in the QS World University Rankings 2027 and Times Higher Education tables. India now holds 143 spots in the latter, the most of any Asian nation. The number of Indian researchers on the Stanford-Elsevier top 2 percent list also grew by double digits.

stories.title: MSU maintains top 10 status for employability
stories.summary: Michigan State University ranked 9th among U.S. public universities in the Global Employability University Ranking 2027. The Times Higher Education list measures how well institutions prepare students for the workplace according to recruiters. The university continues to be a top 10 choice for public school employers.

stories.title: MIT leads Forbes Northeast college rankings
stories.summary: MIT took the top spot in Forbes' latest list of the 25 best colleges in the Northeast. Five other New England schools, including Harvard and Yale, also appeared in the top 10. The region holds an outsized share of the nation's most expensive and elite universities.

stories.title: University of Houston and Rice top Princeton Review
stories.summary: The University of Houston and Rice University have topped the Princeton Review lists for entrepreneurship studies for the eighth consecutive year. The full details of the rankings are available in the original report from The Business Journals.

stories.title: Durham University rises in global league tables
stories.summary: Durham University rose nine places to 85th in the QS World University Rankings 2027. The institution also ranked 49th globally for employer reputation, citing improvements in academic and citation metrics. A record 22 of its subjects are now ranked within the world top 100.

stories.title: Princeton Review names top entrepreneurship schools
stories.summary: The Princeton Review and Entrepreneur have released their 21st annual rankings for undergraduate and graduate entrepreneurship studies. The University of Houston took the top undergraduate spot, while Rice University led the graduate list. The results follow a survey of more than 300 schools.

stories.title: U of T ranks first in Canada for employability
stories.summary: The University of Toronto is ranked first in Canada and 11th in North America for graduate employability by the consultancy Emerging. The survey asks hiring managers which institutions best prepare students for future challenges. The university also placed second among North American public institutions.

stories.title: Himachal Pradesh university debuts in QS rankings
stories.summary: The Central University of Himachal Pradesh has debuted in the QS Asia University Rankings 2027, landing in the 791 to 800 band. The institution is now the top-ranked government university in its home state. It is the university's first appearance in a major global framework.

stories.title: Leiden Ranking includes 45 Iranian universities
stories.summary: The 2026 Leiden Ranking Traditional Edition includes 45 Iranian universities among the top 1,618 institutions globally. The University of Tehran leads the national group. The country remains the most represented nation among Islamic countries for the second consecutive year.

stories.title: UCT MBA program ranks second for sustainability
stories.summary: The University of Cape Town's MBA program has climbed to second place globally in the 2026 Corporate Knights Better World MBA Rankings. The school claims the result proves world-class business education does not require attending institutions like Harvard or MIT.

stories.title: New York college towns ranked by WalletHub
stories.summary: WalletHub has ranked college towns in New York based on affordability, nightlife, and job opportunities. With student living expenses exceeding $39,000 per year, the analysis suggests the surrounding city is a critical factor for student experience. The report highlights the impact of local costs.

stories.title: HKU receives two awards at QS summit
stories.summary: The University of Hong Kong received two awards at the QS Higher Ed Summit in Bali. The school was recognized as the top university in Asia for the second consecutive year and won the Global Engagement Champions Award for its international performance.

stories.title: Ontario teachers union warns of funding pressures
stories.summary: A report from the Ontario Secondary School Teachers' Federation suggests that universities have turned international students into a financial lifeline to offset underfunding. Educators expressed concern about the conditions facing students as they prepare for the next stage of their education.

stories.title: Burnham government faces university funding warnings
stories.summary: Critics warn that Andy Burnham's plan to discount tuition fees for EU students could strain university finances. The policy is intended to facilitate UK participation in the Made in Europe industrial scheme. Ministers fear manufacturing firms could be locked out of supply chains without the deal.

stories.title: British Academy calls for broader graduate metrics
stories.summary: The British Academy argues that current measures of graduate success are too focused on economic outcomes. The body suggests tracking work-life balance, physical health, and job security to provide a complete picture. The current debate remains fixated on whether degrees justify the cost of debt.

stories.title: Transnational framework addresses health inequalities
stories.summary: A new collaborative model aims to bridge the gap between Global North and Global South students through cross-border research. The framework seeks to address international health challenges within undergraduate curricula. It offers a guide for embedding global collaboration into higher education programs.

stories.title: Penn State projects budget deficit
stories.summary: Penn State projects an $87 million year-over-year drop in tuition revenue. The public institution is currently managing a $124 million budget hole following a decline in fall enrollment. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Alvernia University to acquire Marian University
stories.summary: Alvernia University plans to acquire Marian University. The two Catholic institutions stated the merger is based on shared values rather than financial necessity. The campuses are located hundreds of miles apart.

stories.title: Harvard Law students hold silent study-in for clinical instructors
stories.summary: About 40 Harvard Law School students held a silent study-in at Langdell Library on Friday. The group wore blue badges to call on the university to reach a contract agreement with the school clinical instructors. The library remained quiet throughout the hourlong event.

stories.title: Lucy Calkins on AI in the classroom
stories.summary: Columbia University professor Lucy Calkins argues that developing deep reading and writing skills remains essential despite the rise of AI text generation. The full piece is for subscribers. The curriculum creator maintains that children are not a pilot programme for new technology.

stories.title: UK business schools face potential 4.6 billion pound loss
stories.summary: A report by London Economics for the Chartered Association of Business Schools estimates the UK could lose 4.6 billion pounds if international student numbers drop. Each student contributes an average of 103,000 pounds to the economy. The findings highlight the impact of an increasingly challenging policy environment.

stories.title: Stanford students discuss work permit restrictions
stories.summary: The Associated Students of Stanford University held a roundtable to discuss federal restrictions on off-campus work permits. A recent administration memo limits authorizations to students whose work is an integral part of their curriculum. Four higher education groups have filed a lawsuit to block the change.

stories.title: UGC moves to commercialise university research
stories.summary: The University Grants Commission has launched an initiative to commercialise research and innovation within universities. The move aims to bridge the gap between academic output and market application. Further details on the implementation of this commercialisation strategy are currently unavailable.

stories.title: Young people turn to AI for low-risk advice
stories.summary: Research from The Rithm Project suggests young people use AI for emotional support because they perceive it as less risky than human confidants. A survey of nearly 2,400 individuals found that users do not necessarily trust the technology to seek its advice. Relationships are being outsourced.
